rationale: The Court will hold that if removal was proper when effected, post-removal amendment dropping the federal claim does not create a § 1447(c) jurisdictional defect requiring remand; instead, the district court retains authority and may remand only through discretionary supplemental-jurisdiction principles under § 1367(c) and Cohill. Expect the opinion to emphasize the time-of-removal/stability rule (St. Paul Mercury) while underscoring that remand will often be appropriate as a discretionary matter once only state-law claims remain.
